title: Chemotherapy Pharmacology — Resistance and Toxicity Management

segments.label: 01 / 12 · HOOK
title: THE DOSE WAS CORRECT.
THE PATIENT NEARLY DIED.
segments.body_html:
STANDARD DOSE→DPYD VARIANT→FUNCTIONAL OVERDOSE

Nobody miscalculated. The error was conceptual: treating the dose as a property of the drug rather than of the drug in this patient.

beats.text: Five days after starting capecitabine at the protocol dose, she is back in the emergency department. Violent diarrhea. Mouth ulcers. A neutrophil count near zero. She looks like someone who received many times the intended dose. She received exactly the dose the protocol specified. The error was not arithmetic. It was conceptual: treating the dose as a fixed property of the drug rather than of the drug in this patient.

segments.label: 02 / 12 · THE STAKES
title: A MILLIGRAM IS NOT A MILLIGRAM
UNTIL IT ENTERS A SPECIFIC BODY.
segments.body_html:
ADME

What the tumor and normal tissues actually see depends on absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion — and each process varies between patients, sometimes by a factor of five or ten.

beats.text: A prescribed milligram is intent. What the tumor and normal tissues actually see depends on how that milligram is absorbed, where it distributes, how quickly it is metabolized, and how efficiently it is excreted. Every one of those processes varies between patients, sometimes by a factor of five or ten. This chapter is about that variation, and about the resistance and toxicity that follow from it.

segments.label: 03 / 12 · ADME
title: FOUR STEPS DECIDE
WHAT THE TUMOR SEES.
segments.body_html:
ABSORPTIONIV bypasses gut — oral agents cross the gut wall, survive first-pass extraction; a heavy meal changes the functional dose
DISTRIBUTIONProtein binding, lipid solubility, blood-brain barrier — the brain is a sanctuary site where plasma-level drug never arrives
METABOLISMLiver CYP450s inactivate most drugs; prodrugs (cyclophosphamide, capecitabine, irinotecan) require activation first
EXCRETIONCisplatin — kidneys. Doxorubicin — bile. Wrong organ fails → drug accumulates → toxicity

beats.text: Pharmacokinetics gives us the acronym ADME. Absorption: most chemotherapy is intravenous, so variability is minimal — but oral agents like capecitabine must cross the gut wall, survive the liver's first pass, and do so consistently across patients with different food intake. Distribution: highly protein-bound drugs leave more free drug in a malnourished patient with low albumin. The blood-brain barrier is a sanctuary site, blocking drugs even when plasma concentrations are therapeutic. Metabolism: prodrugs like cyclophosphamide and irinotecan require hepatic activation — impaired activation changes the effective dose. Excretion: cisplatin clears through the kidney, doxorubicin through bile. Knowing which organ clears a drug is the minimum requirement for safe prescribing when organs aren't working normally.

segments.label: 04 / 12 · PHARMACOGENOMICS
title: ONE GENE
CHANGES EVERYTHING ABOUT A DOSE.
segments.body_html:
DPYD / fluoropyrimidines3–5% of patients carry loss-of-function variants — standard 5-FU dose becomes a functional overdose; fatalities occur; European countries now mandate pre-treatment testing
UGT1A1 / irinotecanUGT1A1*28 variant impairs SN-38 glucuronidation — active metabolite accumulates → severe neutropenia and diarrhea; genotyping supported by regulatory labeling
TPMT / thiopurines10% of patients carry heterozygous variants — impaired inactivation of active nucleotides → prolonged myelosuppression; genotyping is established clinical practice

beats.text: For a small number of chemotherapy drugs, genetic variation is not a modest modifier — it is the difference between a therapeutic dose and a life-threatening one. Three pairs define the field. DPYD and fluoropyrimidines: three to five percent of the population carries loss-of-function variants that reduce clearance of 5-fluorouracil and its prodrugs; the standard dose accumulates to toxic concentrations; fatalities have occurred. U G T 1 A 1 and irinotecan: the *28 variant impairs clearance of SN-38, the active metabolite, causing severe neutropenia and diarrhea. TPMT and thiopurines: loss-of-function variants impair inactivation of the active nucleotide pool, causing prolonged myelosuppression. The lesson generalizes: for drugs whose safety depends on a specific enzyme, the dose is a property of the drug and that enzyme's activity in this patient.

segments.label: 05 / 12 · RESISTANCE — MECHANISMS
title: SURVIVORS OF TREATMENT
ARE THE MOST RESISTANT.
segments.body_html:
RESPOND→SELECTION→RESISTANT CLONES EXPAND

Resistance can be intrinsic — present before the first dose — or acquired under treatment. The mechanisms are multiple and almost always coexist.

beats.text: A cancer that responds to chemotherapy is not cured unless every cell is killed. The cells that survive treatment are, almost by definition, the least sensitive. Under selection pressure, those cells expand, and the resulting population is more resistant than the original. This is clonal evolution applied to treatment — the dominant reason cancers that initially respond eventually progress. Resistance can be intrinsic, present before the first dose, or acquired under treatment. The mechanisms are multiple and almost always coexist.

segments.label: 06 / 12 · RESISTANCE — SIX DEFENSES
title: SIX PARALLEL DEFENSES
IN ONE CELL.
segments.body_html:
REDUCED UPTAKEtransporter lost — methotrexate never enters
INCREASED EFFLUXP-glycoprotein pumps out taxanes, anthracyclines, vinca — one pump, many drugs
INACTIVATIONglutathione neutralizes alkylators; cytidine deaminase converts analogs
TARGET ALTEREDthymidylate synthase upregulated; topoisomerase II mutated
ENHANCED REPAIRMGMT removes temozolomide adducts; ERCC1 fixes cisplatin crosslinks; BRCA reversion restores HR
APOPTOSIS EVASIONTP53 mutation, BCL-2 overexpression — damage sustained without death

beats.text: Six mechanisms recur. Reduced uptake: cells that downregulate a transporter never let the drug in — methotrexate depends on the reduced folate carrier. Increased efflux: P-glycoprotein pumps out taxanes, anthracyclines, and vinca alkaloids simultaneously — one mechanism, cross-resistance to unrelated drug classes. Drug inactivation: glutathione neutralizes alkylators; cytidine deaminase destroys analogs. Target alteration: thymidylate synthase upregulation blocks fluoropyrimidines; topoisomerase mutations block anthracyclines. Enhanced DNA repair: MGMT removes temozolomide adducts; ERCC1 fixes cisplatin crosslinks; BRCA reversion mutations restore homologous recombination after PARP inhibitor pressure. Apoptosis evasion: TP53 mutation and BCL-2 overexpression let cells survive DNA damage that should have triggered death.

segments.label: 07 / 12 · RESISTANCE — WHY SINGLE TARGETS FAIL
title: BLOCKING ONE PUMP
LEAVES FIVE OTHERS RUNNING.
segments.body_html:
P-gp INHIBITORSreversed pump in the lab
⇄
CLINICAL TRIALS FAILEDtoxicity from normal P-gp blockade + parallel resistance routes intact

Resistance in clinical tumors is a system of overlapping mechanisms. The productive frame is not "block the pump" but "which combination of mechanisms drives this tumor, and does any of them create a new vulnerability?"

beats.text: P-glycoprotein inhibitors were developed and tested through the 1990s and 2000s. They failed to improve outcomes. The failure taught two things. First, inhibiting P-glycoprotein in normal gut and liver tissue altered drug pharmacokinetics in ways that increased systemic toxicity rather than selectively reversing tumor resistance. Second, and more fundamentally, resistance in clinical tumors is not a single-pump problem. Other A B C transporters, enhanced DNA repair, apoptosis evasion — blocking one efflux pump left the others operating. The tumor had multiple routes around the block. Resistance is a system of overlapping mechanisms, not a single leverage point.

segments.label: 08 / 12 · MYELOSUPPRESSION
title: THE NADIR WINDOW
IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY.
segments.body_html:
DOSE DAY 1→NADIR DAY 7–14→RECOVERY DAY 21
Febrile neutropenia (<500 ANC + fever) = empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics NOW — do not wait for cultures.

beats.text: Myelosuppression is the dominant dose-limiting toxicity for most conventional chemotherapy. Bone marrow contains rapidly dividing precursor cells — chemotherapy does not distinguish them from tumor. After a dose, circulating mature cells die off without replacement, and counts fall. The nadir — the lowest point — occurs roughly seven to fourteen days after most regimens; by day twenty-one counts typically recover, which is why twenty-one-day cycles are so common. The clinical emergency is febrile neutropenia: fever with a neutrophil count below five hundred. Infection by normal flora can progress to sepsis rapidly with no reserve to contain it. Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics must start immediately — before culture results — because delaying costs lives.

segments.label: 09 / 12 · NEUROPATHY & NAUSEA
title: TWO TOXICITIES,
TWO DIFFERENT LOGICS.
segments.body_html:
PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHYPlatinum, taxanes, vinca, bortezomib — cumulative and largely irreversible. No pharmacological prevention. Dose reduction or stopping is the management.
CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED NAUSEACisplatin = highly emetogenic. Modern prophylaxis: 5-HT3 antagonist + NK1 antagonist + olanzapine + dexamethasone. Key insight: treat BEFORE cycle one — anticipatory nausea is nearly untreatable once conditioned.

beats.text: Two other toxicities shape clinical management in opposite ways. Peripheral neuropathy from platinum compounds, taxanes, vinca alkaloids, and bortezomib is cumulative — it worsens with each cycle and does not fully reverse when the drug is stopped. There is no established pharmacological prevention; dose modification or discontinuation remains the only management. Completing an effective regimen may produce permanent functional impairment that outlasts the cancer. Nausea is different. Cisplatin was so emetogenic that patients refused treatment. Modern regimens combining a 5-HT3 antagonist, an NK1 antagonist, olanzapine, and dexamethasone have transformed this. The key is prophylaxis before cycle one: anticipatory nausea, conditioned after a bad first experience, is nearly impossible to treat once established.

segments.label: 10 / 12 · SUPPORTIVE CARE PLAN
title: THE CALENDAR IS NOT PAPERWORK.
IT IS THE PLAN.
segments.body_html:
G-CSF PROPHYLAXISPegfilgrastim once per cycle — indicated when febrile neutropenia risk exceeds ~20% from regimen or patient factors. Not routine for all — bone pain, rare splenic rupture, and cost.
CISPLATIN SUPPORTIVE PLAN5-HT3 + NK1 + olanzapine + dexamethasone before and after infusion; pre- and post-hydration for renal protection; magnesium replacement (cisplatin causes renal wasting); blood count check day 10–12; fever instructions for the nadir window
LOGICEach element is a prediction based on known biology — acted on before the problem manifests

beats.text: For any emetogenic or myelosuppressive regimen, the supportive-care plan is written before the first dose — not assembled reactively as problems arise. For a highly emetogenic platinum regimen: five-H-T-3 antagonist, N-K-1 antagonist, dexamethasone, and olanzapine before and after each infusion, tapered over days for the delayed phase. Pre- and post-hydration for renal protection, with magnesium replacement because cisplatin causes renal wasting. G-CSF when febrile neutropenia risk exceeds twenty percent — not routinely, because the drug has its own side effects. A dated calendar: chemotherapy day one, antiemetic taper through day four, blood count check at days ten to twelve, emergency fever instructions for the nadir window, cycle two on day twenty-two after count recovery confirmed. Each element is a prediction based on known biology, acted on before the problem manifests.

segments.label: 11 / 12 · THE THESIS
title: THE PROTOCOL IS THE STARTING POINT.
THE PLAN IS EVERYTHING AFTER.
segments.body_html:
The dose is not a property of the drug. It is a property of the drug and the patient's biology together — their enzyme activity, their organ function, their tumor's resistance mechanisms, and the supportive care plan that makes delivery survivable.

Still open: which combinations of resistance mechanisms drive each specific tumor, and whether any of them create a new exploitable vulnerability.

beats.text: The chapter's claim runs through every section. The dose is not a property of the drug — it is a property of the drug and the patient's biology together. Their enzyme activity: DPYD status before fluoropyrimidines, renal function before cisplatin, liver function before doxorubicin. Their tumor's resistance mechanisms: not a single pump to block, but a system of parallel defenses that requires asking which combination is driving resistance in this specific tumor and whether any creates a new vulnerability. And the supportive care plan that makes delivery of the dose survivable. The protocol number is the starting point. The plan is everything that happens after.

segments.label: 12 / 12 · CLOSE
title: KNOW THE DRUG'S PHARMACOLOGY.
KNOW THIS PATIENT'S BIOLOGY.
segments.body_html:
ADME GOVERNS EXPOSURE//GENES RESHAPE THE DOSE//SELECTION BREEDS RESISTANCE//SUPPORT MAKES DELIVERY POSSIBLE

Cancer Research · Chapter 11 · Chemotherapy Pharmacology — Resistance and Toxicity Management

beats.text: That's the frame. ADME governs what the patient's body does to the drug — and every step varies. Pharmacogenomics tells you when an inherited variant changes safe to lethal at a standard dose. Resistance is clonal evolution under selection pressure, running through parallel mechanisms that rarely yield to a single-target block. And supportive care is not an afterthought — it is the plan that makes the dose deliverable. Know the drug's pharmacology. Know this patient's biology. The two together are the prescription.
